body.statement: Fix \((P,B^0,\varepsilon,\pi_0)\in\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{pub}}\) and its observed moments \(\mathcal O_G\). Let \(\rho\) and \(\rho'\) be full-lattice prefixes ending at the same removed set \(A\). Then \(F(\rho)=F(\rho')\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Comp}(\rho)=\operatorname{Comp}(\rho')\). Moreover, if \(F(\rho)\ne F(\rho')\), then \(\operatorname{Comp}(\rho)\cap\operatorname{Comp}(\rho')=\varnothing\), and the legal suffix paths depend only on \(A\).
body.proof_tex:
Every ordering of \(V\setminus A\) is a legal suffix in the full removed-set
lattice, so suffix legality depends only on \(A\). Write such a suffix as
\((r_1,\ldots,r_{p-|A|})\) and set \(A_0=A\) and
\(A_s=A_{s-1}\cup\{r_s\}\). By
\(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), this suffix contributes, in
immutable original row labels,
\[
 \beta(A_0,r_1),\ \beta(A_1,r_2),\ \ldots,\
 \beta(A_{p-|A|-1},r_{p-|A|}).
 \tag{16}
\]
Every row in (16) depends only on the fixed observed marginals and the
displayed predecessor set. Thus the same suffix appends the same rows to
\(F(\rho)\) and \(F(\rho')\), proving
\[
 F(\rho)=F(\rho')\Longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Comp}(\rho)=\operatorname{Comp}(\rho').
 \tag{17}
\]

Conversely, all completion sets are nonempty because every full-lattice
prefix has a suffix. If one tuple \(T\) belongs to both completion sets,
no assigned row is overwritten, and
\(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\) shows that the projection of
\(T\) onto original rows indexed by \(A\) is both \(F(\rho)\) and
\(F(\rho')\). Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Comp}(\rho)\cap\operatorname{Comp}(\rho')\ne\varnothing
 \Longrightarrow F(\rho)=F(\rho').
 \tag{18}
\]
Equality of nonempty completion sets implies an intersection, so (18) gives
the reverse implication in (17); its contrapositive gives the asserted
disjointness.
body.justification: Right congruence proves that equal full-lattice fragments have exactly the same numerical futures and that unequal fragments never collide later.
body.gap: Generic local-color quotient results do not establish covariance-dependent equality of LiMVAM coefficient rows.
body.consumer: The full-lattice enumerator can merge factorially many order prefixes without dropping a coefficient tuple.
